title: fix(scripts): check-upstream-port-parity ends without discarding its own output (objectui#10006)
body:
Fixes #10006

`scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` ended on `process.exit(...)`. On POSIX, `process.stdout` is
asynchronous when it is a **pipe** (synchronous only for files and TTYs), and `process.exit`
terminates the process while queued output is still queued. `--list` is nothing but a `console.log`
loop, so a piped caller received the listing cut at a point set by how fast it drained — and the
gate's own wiring test captures it with `execFileSync`.

A lost line therefore failed as ``no listing line for ID under FILE``: a specific, confident and
**false** claim about a file the branch under test had never touched. Four unrelated pull requests
were reddened that way — one ejected from the merge queue, one a comment-only diff with no
executable change at all, one a `domain:ui` PR outside the lane that filed the card. The control
already on the record: the same commit `0a4bf6deb`, no new commits and no rebase, went red and then
green.

## The change

The entrypoint sets `process.exitCode` and lets Node exit once the streams drain. This is ⛔ not a
safe substitution in general — it honours the code only if nothing keeps the event loop alive and
nothing after it can run — so both conditions are argued at the site: the gate is fully synchronous
(`readFileSync`/`writeFileSync` only; no timer, socket, child process or handle of any kind) and the
block is the last statement in the module. A pending write to stdout is itself a referenced handle,
so the loop stays alive precisely until the listing has drained.

The repair order is the one this repo states: **remove the construct that permits the error** first,
then make the correct form the only spelling, and only last add a check. Nothing retries a read and
nothing sleeps.

## Exit codes are the gate's verdict — proven unchanged, path by path

Measured over a synthetic ROOT built from the real pin and the real ported files, with the pristine
gate and then with the fixed gate, same commands, same order. `out/err` are the captured stdout and
stderr lengths.

| path exercised | before | after | out/err before | out/err after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `--self-test` | 0 | 0 | 694/0 | 694/0 |
| check, clean tree | 0 | 0 | 2135/0 | 2135/0 |
| check, drifted ported file | 1 | 1 | 1687/1134 | 1687/1134 |
| check, structurally unusable pin | 2 | 2 | 0/241 | 0/241 |
| check, pin absent | 2 | 2 | 0/262 | 0/262 |
| check, ported file unreadable | 1 | 1 | 0/1183 | 0/1183 |
| `--list`, clean tree | 0 | 0 | 28424/0 | 28424/0 |
| `--list`, ported file unreadable (uncaught throw) | 1 | 1 | 0/1210 | 0/1210 |
| `--resync`, no upstream path given | 2 | 2 | 0/75 | 0/75 |
| `--resync`, ref is not a 40-hex sha | 2 | 2 | 0/191 | 0/191 |
| `--resync`, ambiguous, no `--path` | 2 | 2 | 0/524 | 0/524 |
| `--resync`, divergences do not apply | 1 | 1 | 0/1555 | 0/1555 |
| `--resync`, governed file, flag absent | 2 | 2 | 0/825 | 0/825 |
| `--resync`, ungoverned file, succeeds | 0 | 0 | 406/0 | 406/0 |

**14 paths, 0 mismatches** — every exit code, every signal, and every stdout/stderr byte count
identical. ⚠️ Read honestly: the first pass showed three rows differing by 1 and 3 bytes, because the
temp directory name is printed inside those messages and `matrix-before` is one character longer
than `matrix-after`. Re-run with equal-length temp paths, the deltas are zero. The uncaught-throw
row matters most: an exception still escapes before the assignment, exactly as it escaped before the
call, so it still exits 1 with its stack.

## The demonstration, not the prose

The shipped listing is ~28 KB. A pipe holds 64 KiB, so **the shipped listing cannot demonstrate
anything** — an unflushed writer delivers it intact, locally, every time. That is why the card could
only be caught in CI. The new test drives the gate over a **synthetic pin** whose listing is ~1.2 MB
and measures the piped capture against the *same run's capture to a file*, which is synchronous on
POSIX and therefore whole by construction.

Unfixed gate, this shape, three consecutive runs: **96,217 / 175,153 / 161,703** bytes received of
the same 957,139-byte listing, **exit 0 every time**. Three runs, three different cut points, caller
told it succeeded. Fixed gate, same three runs: **957,139 / 957,139 / 957,139**, nothing missing.

⭐ That reproduces the observation the card rests on. Nothing about the tree changes between those
runs; only how much of the queue escaped does. Any explanation that cannot produce red-then-green on
one commit is not the explanation, and this one produces it on demand.

## Ablation — the new pins can fail

Both legs mutate a committed tree, verify the write landed on disk, and restore with
`git checkout HEAD --` verified by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- **A — put the old construct back.** 2 of 15 red: the source pin, and the pipe pin at
  `748,302 chars received of 1,196,646`. ⚠️ Note which 13 stayed **green**, including the existing
  `--list` assertion this card is about: at 28 KB it cannot see the defect. That is the whole reason
  the new test uses a synthetic pin.
- **B — keep `process.exitCode` and plant one real `process.exit(` call line.** 1 of 15 red, and it
  is the source scan itself, naming the planted line. B exists because A tripped the source pin's
  *control leg* first, so A alone would not have shown the scan working.

## Gates

`pnpm lint:root` (the full root scope, 13.5s) · `pnpm type-check:scripts` · `pnpm exec vitest run
scripts/` (178 files, 5288 tests) · `check-upstream-port-parity` both legs · `check-entry-guard` ·
`check-lint-coverage` · `check-lint-rule-coverage` · `check-control-bytes` · `check-test-path-roots`
· `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` · `check-shell-escape-residue` · `check-bash32-floor` ·
`check-changeset-{presence,claims,no-major,overwrite,fixed}` · `check-pending-changeset-literals` ·
`check-vi-mock-{override-shape,specifiers,inherit}` · `check-governed-queue-guard --self-test` ·
`check-unreferenced-sources` — **all exit 0**.

⭐ A single green run proves nothing about a load-dependent truncation, so the wiring test was run
**30 times** (3 concurrent streams of 10) with three added spinners on a 4-CPU box: load average
3.46 before, 9.34 during, 14.78 at the end. **30/30 green, 15 passed each time, 0 non-zero exits.**

`check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports no changeset is owed (no published source moved). The
changeset added is the empty-frontmatter form — the explicit "no release" declaration this repo
treats as a first-class pass.

## ⚠️ This is a class, and this pull request deliberately fixes one member

89 of 107 scanned scripts carry a non-comment `process.exit(`. That number is not actionable on its
own; what matters is the intersection with "prints more than a pipe holds". Measured just now:

⭐ **`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` is a live second instance.** It prints **103,937
chars** — past the 64 KiB threshold — and ends on `process.exit(main(...))`. Five piped runs of the
identical command, taken on this box: **70,757 / 25,656 / 27,132 / 103,937 / 103,937**. Three of
five truncated, at three different points. It is not fixed here — out of scope — and the finding is
being reported for a separate card. Today its consumer imports its `judge` export rather than
spawning it, so nothing is red from it yet; that is timing, not safety.
